description.narrative: (Philippines): .With Water and Sustainable Landscapes-earmarked funds, USAID, through the Safe Water activity, will improve access to resilient water supply and sanitation (WSS) services and sustainable water resources management in water-stressed areas in Palawan, Negros Occidental, and Sarangani. USAID will support local government units (LGUs) and water service providers (WSPs) to expand services and access to financing. To enhance the financial and operational viability and improve service quality of WSPs, USAID will assist in chlorination, pressure management, well drilling and construction supervision, water safety planning, and strategic planning. USAID will also help scale microloan programs to enable wider access to WSS. USAID will support LGUs to develop and implement integrated water security plans to attract WSS investments. USAID aligns with the Philippine Water Supply and Sanitation Master Plan and the Unified Resource Allocation Framework (URAF), which aim to accelerate investments, establish effective WSS bodies, and strengthen regulation of water utilities and resources. USAID will also pilot the Centralized Management System, which places WSPs under LGU oversight to improve operations and ensure the use of common standards and rational tariffs to improve cost recovery. These interventions will enhance LGU eligibility to receive funds under URAF. ..USAID's support for water security plans will drive investments in forest protection and watershed management. USAID will help reconstitute watershed management councils, build operational capacities, develop local watershed conservation plans, set up payments for ecosystem services, bolster forest patrolling, and develop sustainable livelihoods. USAID will also work with the National Water Resources Board to develop a water demand management policy. USAID will document best water efficiency practices and work with the private sector to facilitate its adoption by commercial water users..
